title: Measured-router closure for the corrected score32 NoC Phase 2 schedule
hypothesis: A bounded closure consumer can use the measured single-router clock to form a conservative no-reroute timing upper bound and quantify router-only component accounting without over-claiming full 4x4 mesh PPA.

direct_comparison.primary_question: What changes when the corrected score32 Phase 2 schedule is recosted with the measured segmented-router primitive, and which physical gaps still remain explicit?
include: Use only l2_decoder_attention_score32_noc_phase2_schedule_llama7b_v1_r1 as the schedule source.
Use only l1_segmented_xy_mesh_noc_phase1_v1_r7 as the router primitive source.
Use the measured router critical path to form a conservative no-reroute NoC drain-time upper bound.
Report router area only as a lower bound and router power only as an activity-dependent component estimate.
exclude: Do not linearly claim aggregate 4x4 placed-mesh PPA from a single-router measurement.
Do not hide wiring, congestion, endpoint SRAM, HBM/DRAM, or root-finalizer compute gaps.
Do not update architecture rankings in this bounded sidecar.

expected_benefit: Closes the immediate router-clock abstraction on the corrected Phase 2 schedule.
Makes the remaining full-mesh, SRAM, and HBM gaps explicit before any rerank.
Provides a stable closure artifact that downstream ranking work can consume only after real outputs merge.
risks: The no-reroute timing result is intentionally conservative and cannot replace a release-conversion and mesh rerun at the measured clock.
The router area lower bound and power estimate are component accounting only and are not substitutes for full-fabric PPA.

expected_result.reason: The result should quantify a conservative no-reroute drain-time upper bound, router-area lower bound, and activity-dependent router-power estimate while keeping remaining physical gaps explicit.
